name: MGX

summary.text: MGX is an Abu Dhabi AI investment company launched in March 2024 by Mubadala Investment Company and the technology group G42, chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE's national security adviser. It has invested in OpenAI and xAI and is a founding partner, with OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle, of the Stargate data-center project announced in January 2025.

facts.claim: In October 2024 MGX took part in OpenAI's $6.6 billion funding round at a $157 billion valuation, led by Thrive Capital, and in November 2024 it took part in xAI's $6 billion round at a $50 billion valuation.
facts.quote: In October 2024, MGX took part in OpenAI's $6.6 billion round, which valued the company at $157 billion.

facts.claim: Stargate, announced in January 2025 by OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and MGX, is designed to put up to $500 billion into AI data centers in the United States by 2029; MGX's share was reported at about $7 billion.
facts.quote: Stargate was announced in January 2025 by OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle, and MGX, and is designed to put up to $500 billion into AI data centers in the United States by 2029.

facts.claim: On March 12, 2025 MGX and Binance announced that MGX would invest $2 billion in Binance for a minority stake, paid in stablecoins, described as the first institutional investment in the exchange; the announcement did not say which stablecoin would be used. On May 1, 2025 Eric Trump and World Liberty Financial co-founder Zach Witkoff said at Token2049 in Dubai that the investment would be settled in WLF's USD1 stablecoin, which had launched on March 25, 2025.
facts.quote: The investment grants MGX a minority stake in Binance.

MGX Says $2 Billion Binance Investment Used USD1 Because Of 'Compliance History'

facts.claim: Forbes reported in October 2025 that MGX said it used USD1 for the Binance investment because of the stablecoin's 'compliance history'. On June 10, 2025 Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jeff Merkley wrote to MGX CEO Ahmed Yahia Al Idrissi and Binance CEO Richard Teng asking them to preserve and provide documents on who proposed using USD1 and whether any inducements were offered, stating that the company had confirmed the transaction would likely have been settled in fiat currency had USD1 not been available. The letter states the senators' concerns, not findings; responses were not made public.
facts.quote: the company confirmed that MGX and Binance would have likely settled the transaction in fiat currency if USD1 had not been available

facts.claim: On May 13, 2025 the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security announced it had initiated rescission of the January 2025 'AI Diffusion Rule', which had imposed a worldwide licensing framework on advanced AI chips and was due to take effect May 15, 2025. Under Secretary Jeffery Kessler instructed BIS enforcement officials not to enforce the rule, BIS said it would publish a Federal Register notice formalizing the rescission and issue a replacement rule later, and it issued guidance stating that using Huawei Ascend chips anywhere in the world risks violating U.S. export controls.
facts.quote: Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security Jeffery Kessler has instructed BIS enforcement officials not to enforce the Biden Administration's AI Diffusion Rule

sources.title: Department of Commerce Rescinds Biden-Era Artificial Intelligence Diffusion Rule, Strengthens Chip-Related Export Controls
Department of Commerce formally rescinds AI Diffusion Rule, says deploying Huawei Ascend chips violates US export rules

facts.claim: During the president's May 2025 visit to Abu Dhabi, Reuters reported that the United States had a preliminary agreement with the UAE allowing it to import up to 500,000 of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips a year, with a draft allocating 20 percent (100,000 a year) to G42 and the rest to U.S. companies building data centers in the UAE; the agreement was still being negotiated. In October 2025 BIS issued export licenses for Nvidia chips under the US-UAE AI Acceleration Partnership framework, with the initial permits reported to exclude G42.
facts.quote: The draft called for 20% of the chips, or 100,000 per year, to go to G42.

facts.claim: In May 2025 G42, which co-founded MGX with Mubadala, announced Stargate UAE with OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia, SoftBank and Cisco: a 1-gigawatt AI cluster within a 5-gigawatt UAE-U.S. AI campus in Abu Dhabi. On November 19, 2025 the Commerce Department authorized G42 to buy the equivalent of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell GB300 chips, conditioned on security and reporting requirements.
facts.quote: Both companies are receiving approvals to purchase the equivalent of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips (GB300s).

openQuestions: MGX's fund size is reported variously as a $100 billion target and as a $49 billion close (Tech Times, July 2026); neither was confirmed from MGX itself.
Reports that MGX co-led OpenAI's 2026 round and joined xAI's Series E were not verified.
The sources here are trade press and explainers; MGX's own announcements should be clipped.
MGX's and Binance's own March 12, 2025 release pages (mgx.ae, binance.com) were not reached by the search crawler; the deal terms are recorded from CNBC and CoinDesk coverage of the joint release.
